Seattle historically possesses a mild marine climate, so maximum temperatures reaching near 36°C (96.8°F) represent extreme heat events that pose significant risks to public health, particularly because many residential buildings in the region historically lack air conditioning.
These peak summer temperatures in July and August drive critical decisions for energy grid operators managing surge demand for cooling.
Additionally, understanding these temperature thresholds is vital for water resource managers predicting mountain snowpack runoff and managing municipal water supplies.
